mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by 1% or more for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive monthly INDPRO declines of 1% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between monthly changes in real personal income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) and S&P 500 returns over the prior 12 months suggests that continued income growth will sustain consumer spending and drive further equity gains over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly GDPC1 growth and subsequent 5-day S&P 500 returns breaks down (p > 0.10) or turns negative in a future 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 6-month averages indicates a labor market expansion with slack, which boosts consumer demand and corporate hiring, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed 6-month averages
regime_hint: loose labor market with rising employment
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 6-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) of 10% or more above its 3-month moving average signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises by 10% or more above its 3-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during months when HOUST jumps by 10% or more above its 3-month moving average.
